page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by bottom-25% scores in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, along with poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core performance is average, with middle-50% results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth read and write speeds also fall into the average tier, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r5.3xlarge provides a high density of memory relative to compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-threaded CPU performance. Given the 96.0 GB RAM capacity and average multi-core execution, this instance is well-suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, and memory-bound enterprise applications. It is less optimal for high-throughput web serving or intensive single-threaded processing.
